items.headline: U.S. Markets Closed: Recap of July's Wild Finish
items.summary: U.S. equity markets are closed today, Saturday, August 1st. The last trading session on Friday, July 31, 2026, saw a rally to conclude a volatile July. Major indices posted gains driven by strong tech earnings, particularly from Amazon, while concerns about rising oil prices and inflation persisted. The session also saw a significant drop in Apple shares following a lukewarm revenue forecast. Not financial advice.

items.headline: Amazon Surges on Strong Q2 Profit and AWS Growth
items.summary: Amazon.com Inc. stock soared after reporting stronger-than-expected Q2 profit, with its cloud computing business (AWS) showing accelerated growth. This boosted its market cap by a significant margin.

items.headline: Microsoft Leads Tech Rebound After Robust Earnings
items.summary: Microsoft Corporation surged after reporting robust quarterly results, with its Azure business performing well and issuing strong sales and cloud growth forecasts.

items.headline: AXT Inc. Powers Nasdaq with Record Q2 Top Line
items.summary: AXT Inc. saw significant gains following a record-setting top-line beat for its second quarter and a new long-term supplier agreement.

items.headline: Apple Drops on Lackluster Revenue Forecast
items.summary: Apple Inc. shares tumbled after providing a lackluster forecast for upcoming revenue growth, with services and China revenue falling short of expectations.

items.headline: Roblox Corporation Slides to Two-Year Low
items.summary: Roblox Corporation was among the biggest losers, hitting a two-year low amidst market concerns.

items.headline: Lucid Group Experiences Decline Amidst Mixed EV Sentiment
items.summary: Lucid Group saw a notable decline, reflecting mixed investor sentiment within the electric vehicle (EV) sector.

items.headline: Rivian Automotive Falls Despite Revenue Beat
items.summary: Rivian Automotive shares fell even after beating Q2 revenue estimates, as investors focused on profitability concerns and pressure in the EV market.

sections.title: Market News & Sector Insights - Friday, July 31st

items.headline: S&P 500 Q2 Earnings Show Impressive Growth, Led by Tech
items.summary: The Q2 2026 earnings season for the S&P 500 is reporting impressive results, with 86% of companies exceeding EPS estimates. The blended earnings growth rate stands at 47.4%, the highest since Q2 2021. This strong performance is significantly influenced by unusually large positive EPS surprises from companies like Alphabet and Amazon.com. Excluding these two, growth remains robust at 28.8%.

items.headline: U.S. GDP Grows Slower Than Expected in Q2; PCE Declines
items.summary: The U.S. GDP grew at an annual pace of 1.5% in the second quarter of 2026, slower than the expected 2% and the 2.1% growth in Q1. Consumer spending continued to be the biggest engine. The Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) index declined 0.1% month-over-month in June, though it rose 3.7% year-over-year.

items.headline: Tech and Consumer Discretionary Lead Gains, Utilities and Industrials Lag
items.summary: Information Technology and Consumer Discretionary sectors were among the biggest gainers on Friday, with the Information Technology Select Sector SPDR (XLK) up 5.2% and Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) up 1.6%. Seven of the eleven S&P 500 sectors closed in positive territory. Conversely, utilities (-4.22%) and industrials (-2.03%) were the worst-performing sectors for the week.

items.headline: Rising Oil Prices Worsen Inflation Worries
items.summary: Rising oil prices, partly due to the ongoing conflict with Iran, continued to fuel inflation concerns in the bond market, leading Treasury yields to climb. Crude oil futures ended the day up around 1.17%. Major oil companies like Chevron and Exxon Mobil reported strong Q2 earnings, benefiting from the higher crude prices.

items.headline: AI Investment Continues to Drive Tech Sector
items.summary: Big Tech's massive investments in artificial intelligence continue to translate into significant profits, with Amazon's cloud computing business showing accelerated growth. AI buildout is also bolstering hiring in the nonresidential construction sector. The European Commission announced that the EU's AI Act will begin enforcing transparency rules from August 2.
